problem_text:
A logistics coordinator needs to assign shipments to identical cargo planes. Shipments:
* Component A: volume 44 cubic meters
* Component B: volume 37 cubic meters
* Component C: volume 33 cubic meters
* Component D: volume 54 cubic meters
* Component E: volume 58 cubic meters
* Component F: volume 54 cubic meters
* Component G: volume 68 cubic meters
* Component H: volume 32 cubic meters
* Component I: volume 50 cubic meters
* Component J: volume 31 cubic meters
* Component K: volume 30 cubic meters
* Component L: volume 59 cubic meters
* Component M: volume 46 cubic meters
* Component N: volume 43 cubic meters
* Component O: volume 41 cubic meters
* Component P: volume 59 cubic meters
* Component Q: volume 36 cubic meters
* Component R: volume 55 cubic meters
* Component S: volume 65 cubic meters
* Component T: volume 33 cubic meters
* Component U: volume 46 cubic meters
* Component V: volume 36 cubic meters
* Component W: volume 38 cubic meters
* Component X: volume 33 cubic meters
* Component Y: volume 30 cubic meters
* Component Z: volume 46 cubic meters
* Component [: volume 57 cubic meters
* Component \: volume 63 cubic meters
* Component ]: volume 67 cubic meters
* Component ^: volume 48 cubic meters
* Component _: volume 34 cubic meters
* Component `: volume 51 cubic meters
* Component a: volume 60 cubic meters

Each cargo plane can carry up to 100 cubic meters of freight. Assign all shipments using the fewest planes. Each shipment must be loaded onto exactly one plane, and the total volume on a plane cannot exceed its capacity.
